name: Gravita India Ltd
tagline: Established lead/aluminium/plastic recycling compounder, high quality but no sharp near-term catalyst at its current size
business_overview: Gravita India is one of India's largest lead recyclers, organised across four verticals: lead recycling (flagship), aluminium recycling, plastic recycling, and turnkey projects, with a growing international manufacturing footprint.
fundamentals_table: Jul 2026 community read: margin compression in plastic segment (EBITDA margin 19.97%->14.17% QoQ) and copper segment; capacity utilization flat ~65-75% for 3 quarters running
fundamentals_narrative: Genuinely strong quality metrics (high ROE, low debt, real double-digit growth) with a credible secular circular-economy tailwind, but recent quarters show margin pressure in the newer plastic and copper segments and capacity utilization has plateaued, with a pending MCX aluminium-exchange listing as the main near-term catalyst still awaited.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 243 available posts (Aug 2025-Aug 2026). Sentiment has been steady and analytical throughout, dominated by detailed concall Q&A on capacity utilization, the pending MCX aluminium listing, and segment-level margin dynamics - no major bull or bear inflection, just routine ongoing tracking.
community_signal: No VP-trusted-tier user posted in the read window. Non-trusted posters (Krishna_Kumar, A.R_PAWAR, hirakroy123, Rahul_Parmar) tracked routine but real concerns: flat capacity utilization (~65-75%) for three consecutive quarters, a pending MCX aluminium-exchange approval still not finalised as of early 2026, and margin compression in the plastic (Jul 2026) and copper (Aug 2026) segments most recently.
bull_case: Strong, real quality metrics: 22.56% ROE, low debt, net cash position, 20% 3-year sales growth
Secular circular-economy/recycling tailwind with an established, diversified (lead/aluminium/plastic/copper) international footprint
Pending MCX aluminium-exchange listing could unlock a new domestic volume channel once approved
bear_case: Capacity utilization has been flat (~65-75%) for three consecutive quarters - the company is not yet 'sweating its assets' as one community member put it
Recent margin compression in both the plastic segment (Jul 2026) and copper segment (Aug 2026) - two of the newer growth verticals

At ~Rs 13,446 Cr market cap with ~20% trailing growth, a 10x-in-2-3-years or 100x-in-10-years outcome would require a much sharper catalyst than currently visible - this looks more like a steady 15-20% compounder than an explosive multibagger from here
verdict_headline: High-quality recycling compounder, but sized and growing too steadily for this project's aggressive thesis without a sharper catalyst
verdict_reasoning: Fundamentals clear the quality gate cleanly (ROE, debt, growth) but the growth rate (~20% CAGR) does not mathematically support a 10x-in-2-3-years or 100x-in-10-years outcome absent a major re-rating catalyst
Recent-quarter margin pressure in newer segments (plastic, copper) and stagnant capacity utilization argue against calling this an inflection point right now
Medium conviction reflects genuine business quality, but thesis_fit is 'neither' given the mismatch between growth rate and this project's return bar

four_box.note: Secular circular-economy/recycling tailwind with a diversified international footprint is real and structural; capacity utilization flat ~65-75% for 3 consecutive quarters ('not sweating assets') — tam weak; recent margin compression in newer plastic/copper segments undermines confidence in the diversification moat — weak; no valuation data recorded, pending MCX aluminium-exchange listing is the main awaited catalyst — weak.

track_record.note: FY19-FY26 screener consolidated. Both revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same FY: FY22 (+57%, ROCE 31%), FY23 (+26%, 32%), FY24 (+13%, 28%), FY25 (+22%, 22%), FY26 (+10%, 17%). FY19-FY21 missed (ROCE 13-21% with sub-10% or single-digit growth in FY20-FY21). ROCE has fallen from a 32% peak (FY23) to 17% (FY26) as newer plastic/copper verticals dilute and utilisation plateaus.

quality_metrics.note: FY26 ROCE 17%, down from 32% (FY23). Net cash (~Rs 414 Cr, D/E 0.20) despite Rs 736 Cr gross borrowings. OPM range-bound ~8-10%. CFO only Rs 169 Cr FY26 against EBITDA ~Rs 427 Cr - lead/metal recycling is working-capital-heavy and capacity capex has run ahead of a utilisation that has been flat ~65-75% for three quarters ('not sweating assets'), so capex_efficiency neutral.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~32x trailing on a ~15-20% recycling compounder needs ~25% EPS CAGR FY26-28 against a ~18-22x cyclical-industrial exit; capacity utilisation has been flat ~65-75% for three quarters and ROCE has fallen 32%->17%
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: revenue ~Rs 5,000-5,400 Cr (+17-25% on new capacity), OPM ~9-10%, PAT ~Rs 500-560 Cr
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: revenue ~Rs 6,000-6,600 Cr if utilisation lifts and the MCX aluminium channel opens, PAT ~Rs 600-680 Cr
market_expectation.gap_basis: 32x P/E while ROCE fell 32%->17% (FY23->FY26), plastic and copper segment margins compressed (Jul-Aug 2026) and utilisation plateaued. Our FY28 PAT is ~20% below the ~25% CAGR the multiple implies; the pending MCX aluminium listing is the main unpriced catalyst.
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view
